features.claim: It had a big skull on a short neck and a long tail.
features.quote: Allosaurus was a typical large theropod, having a massive skull on a short neck, a long, slightly sloping tail, and reduced forelimbs.

features.claim: Its mouth was full of many sharp teeth with saw-like edges.
features.quote: Its skull was light, robust, and equipped with dozens of sharp, serrated teeth.

features.claim: It had small horns above its eyes.
features.quote: It had three-fingered hands and distinctive horns above its eyes.

features.claim: Its hands had three fingers with big curved claws.
features.quote: The forelimbs of Allosaurus are short in comparison to the hindlimbs (only about 35% the length of the hindlimbs in adults) and have three fingers per hand, tipped with large, strongly curved and pointed claws.

features.claim: Its arms were short next to its big back legs.
features.quote: Its three-fingered forelimbs were smaller than its large hind legs, and the body was balanced by a long, heavy tail.

features.claim: Its body was balanced by a long, heavy tail.
features.quote: Its three-fingered forelimbs were smaller than its large hind legs, and the body was balanced by a long, heavy tail.

features.claim: It had a broad rib cage that made a barrel chest.
features.quote: The rib cage is broad, giving it a barrel chest, especially in comparison to less derived theropods like Ceratosaurus.
The impression shows small scales measuring 1 to 3 millimeters in diameter.

not_this.claim: Old pictures show Allosaurus as a kind of Tyrannosaurus, but that is wrong.
not_this.quote: Allosaurus was depicted as a species of Tyrannosaurus in the 1967 horror film The Beast of Hollow Mountain, and the 1967 film The Valley of Gwangi.

debated.claim: No one knows for sure why Allosaurus had small horns on its skull.
debated.quote: No one knows for sure why Allosaurus had small horns on its skull.

debated.claim: One skin impression might not be from Allosaurus.
debated.quote: However, it has been noted that these scales are more similar to those of sauropods, and due to the presence of non-theropod remains associated with the tail of "Big Al Two" there is a possibility that this skin impression is not from Allosaurus.

second_reading.claim: Allosaurus was a large meat-eating dinosaur that walked on two legs.
second_reading.quote: Allosaurus was a large meat-eating dinosaur that lived in prehistoric North America.

second_reading.claim: People once thought Saurophaganax was a bigger cousin of Allosaurus, but that idea was a mistake.
second_reading.quote: Saurophaganax, a related dinosaur, was once thought to be a larger cousin of Allosaurus. But recent research has shown that Saurophaganax was probably named by mistake, and many of the bones actually belonged to Allosaurus.

second_reading.claim: Scientists are not sure whether Allosaurus hunted in packs or lived alone.
second_reading.quote: Scientists have debated whether Allosaurus had cooperative social behavior and hunted in packs or was a solitary predator that forms congregations, with evidence supporting both arguments.
